22042.q: How long is one lap of the running track in a stadium?
22042.e: One lap of a normal running track measures 400 metres. So for 800 metres you run two laps.
22042.m: One lap of a stadium is 400 metres long.

22043.q: In which city does the famous athletics meeting “Weltklasse” take place in the Letzigrund stadium?
22043.e: Weltklasse Zürich takes place in the Letzigrund stadium. Many of the best athletes in the world compete there.
22043.m: Weltklasse Zürich is a famous athletics meeting.

22044.q: Which Swiss sprinter became European champion over 200 metres in 2022?
22044.e: Mujinga Kambundji from Bern won the 200-metre title in Munich in 2022 and defended it in Rome in 2024. She is one of the fastest Swiss women.
22044.m: Mujinga Kambundji is a fast Swiss sprinter.

22045.q: How many rings are there on the Olympic flag?
22045.e: The five rings stand for five parts of the world that come together at the Games.
22045.m: The Olympic flag has five rings.

22046.q: Which medal does the person in third place get at the Olympic Games?
22046.e: Third place receives a bronze medal. The places before it get more valuable medals.

22047.q: In which country were the Olympic Games held in ancient times?
22047.e: The first Olympic Games took place about 2,800 years ago in Olympia in Greece.
22047.m: The Olympic Games come from Greece.

22048.q: What burns in the stadium during the Olympic Games?
22048.e: The Olympic flame is lit in Greece and carried to the stadium with torches. It burns until the end of the Games.
22048.m: The Olympic flame burns throughout the Games.

22049.q: In which country did the 2026 Winter Olympics take place?
22049.e: The 2026 Winter Games took place in February in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo in Italy.
22049.m: The 2026 Winter Games were in Italy.

22050.q: Which Swiss place has hosted the Winter Olympics twice?
22050.e: St Moritz in the Engadine hosted the Winter Games in 1928 and 1948.
22050.m: St Moritz has hosted the Winter Olympics twice.

22051.q: How many years are there usually between two Summer Olympic Games?
22051.e: The Summer Games take place every four years, for example in Paris in 2024 and in Los Angeles in 2028.
22051.m: The Summer Olympics are held every four years.

22052.q: What is the name of the man who founded the modern Olympic Games?
22052.e: The Frenchman Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympic Games. The first ones took place in Athens in 1896.
22052.m: Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympic Games.

22053.q: What do you play badminton with?
22053.e: In badminton you hit a light object with feathers over a high net. It is called a shuttlecock.
22053.m: Badminton is played with a shuttlecock.

22054.q: What is the board with four small wheels that you ride standing up called?
22054.e: A skateboard is a board with four wheels. You push off with one foot and ride on it.
22054.m: A skateboard has four small wheels.

22055.q: Which ball is used in floorball?
22055.e: The floorball ball is made of plastic and has lots of holes. That makes it light so it does not fly too far.
22055.m: The floorball ball has lots of holes.

22056.q: In which sport do you need a bow and arrow?
22056.e: In archery you shoot at a target with a bow and arrow.
22056.m: In archery you aim with a bow and arrow.

22057.q: What do you slide across the ice in curling?
22057.e: In curling you let a heavy granite stone glide across the ice. Teammates sweep in front of it with brooms.
22057.m: In curling a stone glides across the ice.

22058.q: What do Schwingen wrestlers wear over their clothes so that they can hold on?
22058.e: Schwingen wrestlers wear short trousers made of strong fabric over their clothes. They grab their opponent by them.
22058.m: In Schwingen you grab your opponent by the wrestling shorts.

22059.q: Which piece of sports equipment is a large ring that you spin around your hips?
22059.e: You keep the hula hoop in the air by moving your hips. It takes practice.
22059.m: You spin the hula hoop around your hips.

22060.q: Who makes sure in a game that everyone follows the rules?
22060.e: The referee knows the rules exactly. They blow the whistle when someone commits a foul.
22060.m: The referee makes sure the rules are followed.

22061.q: What is the game called in which one child has to catch the others?
22061.e: In tag one child has to catch the others. Whoever is touched then has to do the catching.
22061.m: In tag you have to catch the others.

22062.q: What do you call it when both teams have the same number of points at the end?
22062.e: If both teams have the same number of goals or points, nobody has won. That is a draw.
22062.m: With the same number of points it is a draw.

22063.q: In volleyball, what is the maximum number of times a team may touch the ball before it must go over the net?
22063.e: In volleyball a team may play the ball at most three times. Then it must go to the other side.
22063.m: In volleyball a team has three touches.

22064.q: How many steps may you take in handball with the ball in your hand?
22064.e: In handball you may take at most three steps with the ball in your hand. After that you must bounce, pass or shoot.
22064.m: In handball three steps with the ball are allowed.

22065.q: What does the referee do to stop the game?
22065.e: The referee stops the game with a blast on the whistle. That way everyone can hear it well.

22066.q: What happens in football when the ball goes completely over the goal line into the goal?
22066.e: A goal only counts when the whole ball is over the line. Then the team is given a goal.
22066.m: A goal counts when the ball is completely over the line.

a: Following the rules and respecting others
22067.e: Fair play means playing honestly, keeping to the rules and respecting your opponent.
22067.m: Fair play means playing honestly and respectfully.

22068.q: What do you do with your opponent after the game?
22068.e: After the game you shake hands with your opponent or give them a high five. That shows respect.
22068.m: After the game you shake hands with your opponent.

22069.q: What do you do if an opponent has been hurt and is lying on the ground?
a: Kick the ball out of play
22069.e: A fair player kicks the ball out of play. That stops the game and the injured player gets help.
22069.m: If someone is injured, you kick the ball out of play.

22070.q: How do you behave fairly when your team has lost?
22070.e: You stay fair even after a defeat. You congratulate the winners on their success.
22070.m: A good loser congratulates the winner.

22071.e: In a dive a player deliberately falls over even though they were not fouled. That is unfair and earns a yellow card.
22071.m: A dive is an unfair trick.

22072.e: Doping means taking banned substances to be stronger or faster. It is unfair and harms your health.

a: They throw things onto the pitch
22073.e: Fair spectators cheer on their team and also respect the opponent and the referee.
22073.m: Fair spectators respect everyone on the pitch.

22074.q: In which ancient sanctuary did the first Olympic Games take place?
22074.e: The ancient Olympic Games were held in Olympia on the Greek peninsula of the Peloponnese. They were dedicated to the god Zeus.
22074.m: The ancient Games took place in Olympia in honour of Zeus.

22075.q: In which year does tradition place the first ancient Olympic Games?
22075.e: According to ancient tradition, the lists of winners at Olympia began in 776 BC. After that the Games were held every four years for more than 1,000 years.
22075.m: According to tradition, the ancient Olympic Games began in 776 BC.

22076.q: In which country was the game of basketball invented in 1891?
22076.e: The PE teacher James Naismith invented basketball in the USA in 1891 as an indoor game for the winter. At first he used peach baskets as the baskets.
22076.m: Basketball was invented in the USA in 1891.

22077.q: Which sport was invented in the USA in 1895 as a game with less body contact than basketball?
22077.e: In 1895 William G. Morgan invented a game without body contact in which the ball is played over a net. That is how volleyball began.
22077.m: Volleyball was invented in the USA in 1895.

22078.q: In which country were the first common football rules laid down in 1863?
22078.e: In 1863 the Football Association was founded in London. It wrote the first shared rules for modern football.
22078.m: England is seen as the home of modern football.

22079.q: When did the first Tour de France take place?
22079.e: The first Tour de France started in 1903 and was organised by the sports newspaper “L'Auto”. Today it is one of the best-known cycling races in the world.
22079.m: The Tour de France has existed since 1903.

22080.q: Which sports federation has its headquarters in Zurich?
22080.e: FIFA was founded in Paris in 1904 and is now based in Zurich. The European football association UEFA, on the other hand, is based in Nyon on Lake Geneva.
22080.m: The world football federation FIFA is based in Zurich.

22081.q: Since when has the Wimbledon tennis tournament been held?
22081.e: The first tournament at Wimbledon took place in 1877. It is the oldest tennis tournament in the world.
22081.m: Since 1877, Wimbledon has been the oldest tennis tournament in the world.

22082.q: Who is considered the founder of the modern Olympic Games?
22082.e: In 1894 the Frenchman Pierre de Coubertin set up the International Olympic Committee. Two years later the first modern Games took place.
22082.m: Pierre de Coubertin founded the modern Olympic Games.

22083.q: Where did the first Olympic Games of modern times take place in 1896?
22083.e: The first modern Games were held in Athens in 1896. This recalled the Greek origin of the Games.
22083.m: The first modern Olympic Games took place in Athens in 1896.

22084.q: In which Swiss city does the International Olympic Committee (IOC) have its headquarters?
22084.e: The IOC has been based in Lausanne since 1915. The Olympic Museum is also there.
22084.m: Lausanne is called the Olympic capital because the IOC is based there.

22085.q: Which Swiss place has hosted the Olympic Winter Games twice?
22085.e: St Moritz hosted the Olympic Winter Games in 1928 and 1948. No other Swiss place has hosted Olympic Winter Games so far.
22085.m: St Moritz hosted the Winter Games in 1928 and 1948.

22086.q: How many rings does the Olympic flag show?
22086.e: The five interlinked rings stand for the continents that are joined together by the Games. The rings are blue, yellow, black, green and red on a white background.
22086.m: The five Olympic rings stand for the continents joined together.

22087.q: Where is the Olympic flame lit for each Games?
a: At the IOC headquarters in Lausanne
22087.e: The flame is lit in Olympia using the sun's rays and a curved mirror. Then a torch relay brings it to the host city.
22087.m: The Olympic flame is lit with sunlight in Olympia.

22088.q: Which cities hosted the Olympic Winter Games in February 2026?
22088.e: The 2026 Winter Games took place in northern Italy, with Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo as the main venues. They were the first Games with two officially named host cities.
22088.m: The 2026 Winter Games took place in Milan and Cortina d'Ampezzo.

22089.q: What does the Olympic motto “Citius, altius, fortius” mean?
22089.e: The Latin motto means “faster, higher, stronger”. In 2021 the word “communiter” was added, which means “together”.
22089.m: The Olympic motto is “faster, higher, stronger, together”.

22090.q: Which country won the first Football World Cup in 1930?
22090.e: The first World Cup took place in Uruguay in 1930. The host Uruguay beat Argentina 4-2 in the final.
22090.m: Uruguay became the first football world champion in 1930.

22091.q: Which country won the 2026 Football World Cup?
22091.e: In the final on 19 July 2026 in New Jersey, Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time. It was Spain's second World Cup title after 2010.
22091.m: Since 2026 Spain has been world champion twice.

22092.q: Which three countries hosted the 2026 Football World Cup together?
22092.e: The 2026 World Cup was the first with three host countries. Most of the matches took place in the USA.
22092.m: The 2026 World Cup was played in the USA, Canada and Mexico.

22093.q: How many teams took part in the 2026 Football World Cup?
22093.e: In 2026 FIFA enlarged the tournament from 32 to 48 teams. This meant there was a round of 32 for the first time.
22093.m: For the first time, 48 teams played at the 2026 Football World Cup.

22094.q: Which country has the most men's Football World Cup titles (as of 2026)?
22094.e: Brazil won the title five times: in 1958, 1962, 1970, 1994 and 2002. Germany and Italy have four titles each.
22094.m: With five titles, Brazil holds the record for football world championships.

22095.q: In which year did Switzerland host the Football World Cup?
22095.e: The 1954 World Cup took place in Switzerland. Germany won the final in Bern against Hungary, which is known as the “Miracle of Bern”.
22095.m: Switzerland hosted the Football World Cup in 1954.

22096.q: In which two Swiss cities did the 2026 men's Ice Hockey World Championship take place?
22096.e: The 2026 Ice Hockey World Championship was held in Zurich and in Fribourg. So Switzerland hosted this tournament once again.
22096.m: The 2026 Ice Hockey World Championship took place in Zurich and Fribourg.

22097.q: Where will the 2027 Alpine World Ski Championships take place?
22097.e: The 2027 World Ski Championships will be held in Crans-Montana in Valais. St Moritz was last the host in 2017.
22097.m: The 2027 Alpine World Ski Championships will take place in Crans-Montana.

22099.q: How long does a regular adult football match last without added time?
22099.e: Two halves of 45 minutes each are played. On top of that comes added time, which the referee decides.
22099.m: A football match lasts two times 45 minutes.

22100.q: From what distance from the goal is a penalty taken?
22100.e: The penalty spot is 11 metres in front of the middle of the goal line. That is why in Germany a penalty is also called an Elfmeter, an “eleven-metre”.
22100.m: A penalty is taken from 11 metres.

22101.q: What does the referee show a player after a second yellow card in the same match?
a: A second yellow and red, which means a sending-off
22101.e: Two cautions in the same match lead to a second yellow card and a red card. The player must leave the pitch and may not be replaced.
22101.m: If you get two yellow cards, you are sent off.

22102.q: When is a goal valid in football?
a: When the ball has completely crossed the goal line
When the ball touches the goal line
When half of the ball is in the goal
When the goalkeeper does not stop the ball
22102.e: The whole of the ball must be over the goal line between the posts and under the crossbar. Goal-line technology can check this.
22102.m: A goal only counts when the ball is completely over the line.

22103.q: At which restart in football is there no offside if a teammate receives the ball directly?
a: At a pass in open play
22103.e: Anyone who receives the ball directly from a throw-in, goal kick or corner kick cannot be offside. The offside rule applies to free kicks and normal passes.
22103.m: There is no offside from a throw-in, goal kick or corner kick.

22104.q: How must a throw-in be taken in football?
a: With both hands from behind and over the head
With one hand from the side
With the foot from the touchline
22104.e: For a throw-in the player holds the ball with both hands and throws it from behind and over the head. Both feet must touch the ground.
22104.m: For a throw-in you throw with both hands over your head.

22105.q: What does the abbreviation VAR stand for in football?
22105.e: VAR stands for “Video Assistant Referee”. It uses video images to check important situations such as goals, penalties and red cards.
22105.m: The VAR helps the referee with video images.

22106.q: How many players from one team are on the court at the same time in basketball?
22106.e: In basketball it is five against five. Substitutions are allowed as often as you like.
22106.m: In basketball it is five against five.

22107.q: At what height does the basketball basket hang?
22107.e: The ring hangs 3.05 metres above the floor. That is exactly 10 feet, as it was with the inventor Naismith.
22107.m: The basketball basket hangs 3.05 metres high.

22108.q: How many points does a basket thrown from outside the three-point line score?
22108.e: Shots from outside the line count for three points, shots from inside for two. A free throw counts for one point.
22108.m: A shot from behind the three-point line scores three points.

22109.q: How many seconds does a team have in basketball to shoot at the basket?
22109.e: The shot clock is 24 seconds. If the shot does not touch the ring in time, the other team gets the ball.
22109.m: In basketball an attack must be finished within 24 seconds.

22110.q: How long does a basketball game last under FIBA rules without overtime?
22110.e: Under the international FIBA rules there are four quarters of ten minutes each. In the American NBA a quarter lasts twelve minutes.
22110.m: A FIBA game has four quarters of ten minutes each.

a: Taking too many steps with the ball in your hands without dribbling
Fouling an opponent who is shooting
Putting a foot on the three-point line
The ball rolling out of play
22111.e: If you are holding the ball, you may only take two steps without dribbling. After that you must pass or shoot, or you may not move any more.
22111.m: With the ball in your hands, only two steps are allowed.

22112.q: After how many personal fouls must a player leave the game under FIBA rules?
22112.e: A player is out with their fifth personal foul. In the NBA it is six fouls.
22112.m: Under FIBA rules a player is out with the fifth foul.

22113.q: How many free throws does a player get if they are fouled during an unsuccessful three-point shot?
22113.e: For a foul during a shot, you get as many free throws as the shot would have scored. So for a three-point shot it is three.
22113.m: A foul on a three-point shot gives three free throws.

22114.q: In tennis, how are points counted within a game after the first point?
22114.e: A game is counted with 15, 30 and 40. With the next point you win the game, unless it is 40 all.
22114.m: In tennis you count 15, 30, 40 and then game.

22115.q: What is the score 40 all called in tennis?
22115.e: At 40 all it is deuce. After that a player needs two points in a row to win the game.

22116.q: How many attempts at a serve does a tennis player have per point?
22116.e: If the first serve is a fault, you may take a second one. If that also fails, it is a double fault and the point goes to the opponent.
22116.m: Two faults on the serve make a double fault.

22117.q: Up to how many points is a normal tie-break played?
22117.e: The tie-break is usually played at 6 games all. The winner is the first to reach 7 points with a lead of at least two points.
22117.m: A tie-break goes to 7 points with a two-point lead.

22118.q: On which surface is the Wimbledon Grand Slam tournament played?
22118.e: Wimbledon is the best-known grass-court tournament in the world. The French Open in Paris is played on clay.

22119.q: How many Grand Slam tournaments are there in tennis each year?
22119.e: The four Grand Slam tournaments are the Australian Open, the French Open, Wimbledon and the US Open. They are the most important tournaments in tennis.
22119.m: There are four Grand Slam tournaments in tennis every year.

22120.q: In tennis, what does the word “let” mean on a serve?
a: The ball touches the net and lands in the correct box
The ball lands behind the baseline
The player steps on the line
22120.e: With a let, the serve touches the top of the net and still falls into the correct box. The serve is then taken again.
22120.m: A let serve is taken again.

22121.q: Which two disciplines are combined in biathlon?
22121.e: In biathlon the athletes race on cross-country skis and shoot at targets in between. For missed shots there is a penalty loop or penalty time.
22121.m: Biathlon combines cross-country skiing with shooting.

22122.q: Which disciplines make up Nordic combined?
22122.e: In Nordic combined the athletes first jump from the ski jump. Then comes a cross-country race.
22122.m: Nordic combined is made up of ski jumping and cross-country skiing.

22123.q: In which position do athletes go down the ice track in skeleton?
22123.e: In skeleton you lie on your front and go head first. In luge, on the other hand, you lie on your back and go feet first.
22123.m: In skeleton you go down on your front, head first.

22124.q: What is the target circle in curling called?
22124.e: The stones are played towards the “house”, a target circle with a centre point. Points are given for stones that are closer to the centre than the opponent's best stone.
22124.m: In curling you aim your stones at the house.

22125.q: How many players from an ice hockey team are normally on the ice at the same time?
22125.e: There are five skaters and one goalkeeper on the ice. For a penalty a player must go to the penalty box.
22125.m: In ice hockey there are five skaters and one goalkeeper on the ice.

22126.q: In which Bernese Oberland village does the well-known Lauberhorn race take place?
22126.e: The Lauberhorn race in Wengen has the longest downhill course in the World Cup. In Adelboden, on the other hand, giant slalom and slalom races take place.
22126.m: The Lauberhorn race takes place in Wengen every year.

22127.q: Which alpine ski discipline has the most gates and the shortest distances between them?
22127.e: In slalom the gates are very close together, so you need lots of quick turns. In downhill there are only a few gates and the highest speed.
22127.m: Slalom is the most technical and tightest discipline in skiing.

22128.q: Which winter sport takes place on the Cresta Run in St Moritz?
22128.e: On the Cresta Run, athletes ride a sled on their front, head first. Today's skeleton developed from this sport.
22128.m: The Cresta Run in St Moritz is the birthplace of skeleton.

22129.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Roger Federer win in his career?
22129.e: Roger Federer won 20 Grand Slam titles, eight of them at Wimbledon. He ended his career in 2022.
22129.m: Roger Federer won 20 Grand Slam singles titles.

22130.q: In which sport did Simon Ammann win four Olympic gold medals?
22130.e: Simon Ammann won both individual ski jumping events in Salt Lake City in 2002 and in Vancouver in 2010. That makes him one of the most successful ski jumpers.
22130.m: Simon Ammann won Olympic gold in ski jumping four times.

22131.q: Which Swiss woman became world champion in the 100 metres hurdles in Tokyo in 2025?
22131.e: In 2025 in Tokyo, Ditaji Kambundji surprisingly won the world title in the 100 metres hurdles. She was the first Swiss outdoor athletics world champion.
22131.m: Ditaji Kambundji became hurdles world champion in 2025.

22132.q: How many times in a row had Marco Odermatt won the overall alpine skiing World Cup by 2026?
22132.e: Marco Odermatt won the overall World Cup five times in a row, from 2022 to 2026. He is one of Switzerland's most successful ski racers.
22132.m: Marco Odermatt won the overall World Cup five times from 2022 to 2026.

22133.q: Which Swiss tennis player won Olympic singles gold in Tokyo in 2021?
22133.e: At the Tokyo Games, Belinda Bencic won gold in the singles and silver in the doubles. Because of the pandemic, the Games only took place in 2021.
22133.m: Belinda Bencic won Olympic gold in tennis in 2021.

22134.q: In which sport did Nino Schurter become Olympic champion in 2016?
22134.e: In Rio in 2016, Nino Schurter won gold in cross-country mountain biking. He has been world champion in this discipline several times.
22134.m: Nino Schurter is a Swiss Olympic mountain bike champion.

22135.q: In which sport did Dario Cologna win four Olympic gold medals?
22135.e: Dario Cologna won Olympic gold in cross-country skiing in 2010, twice in 2014 and in 2018. He comes from the Val Müstair in the Grisons.
22135.m: Dario Cologna is the most successful Swiss cross-country skier.

22136.q: Which Swiss ski racer won the overall World Cup in 2016 and 2024?
22136.e: Lara Gut-Behrami won the big crystal globe in 2016 and again in 2024. Eight years passed between these wins.
22136.m: Lara Gut-Behrami won the overall World Cup twice.

22137.q: Which athlete won four gold medals at the 1936 Olympic Games in Berlin?
22137.e: The American Jesse Owens won the 100 m, the 200 m, the long jump and the relay. His success disproved the Nazis' racial propaganda.
22137.m: Jesse Owens won four gold medals in Berlin in 1936.

22138.q: Which footballer is the only one to have become world champion three times?
22138.e: The Brazilian Pelé won the World Cup in 1958, 1962 and 1970. No other player has won the World Cup title three times.
22138.m: Pelé is the only three-time football world champion.

22139.q: Which gymnast was the first to receive a score of 10.0 at the Olympic Games, in Montreal in 1976?
22139.e: The Romanian Nadia Comăneci, only 14 years old, performed the perfect routine on the uneven bars. The scoreboard could only show “1.00” because nobody had expected a ten.
22139.m: Nadia Comăneci scored the first Olympic ten in 1976.

22140.q: With which team did Michael Jordan win six NBA championships?
22140.e: With the Chicago Bulls, Michael Jordan won the titles from 1991 to 1993 and from 1996 to 1998. Many people see him as the best basketball player of all time.
22140.m: Michael Jordan won six titles with the Chicago Bulls.

22141.q: In which sport did Muhammad Ali become famous?
22141.e: Muhammad Ali was heavyweight boxing world champion three times. His saying “Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee” is well known.
22141.m: Muhammad Ali was one of the most famous boxers in history.

22142.q: How many Grand Slam singles titles did Serena Williams win?
22142.e: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles, more than any other player since 1968. She ended her career in 2022.
22142.m: Serena Williams won 23 Grand Slam singles titles.

22143.q: How many times did Rafael Nadal win the French Open in Paris?
22143.e: Rafael Nadal won at Roland Garros 14 times, more often than anyone else at any Grand Slam tournament. That is why he is called the “King of Clay”.
22143.m: Rafael Nadal won the French Open 14 times.

22144.q: What world record time did Usain Bolt run over 100 metres in Berlin in 2009 (as of 2026)?
22144.e: Usain Bolt ran 9.58 seconds at the 2009 World Championships in Berlin. This world record still stands today.
22144.m: Usain Bolt's 100-metre world record of 9.58 seconds dates from 2009.

22145.q: Which time barrier was broken for the first time in an official race at the London Marathon in April 2026?
22145.e: The Kenyan Sabastian Sawe ran the 2026 London Marathon in 1:59:30. A marathon is more than 42 kilometres long.
22145.m: In 2026 someone ran an official marathon in under two hours for the first time.

22146.q: How many Olympic medals did the swimmer Michael Phelps win in total (as of 2026)?
22146.e: Between 2004 and 2016 Michael Phelps won 28 medals in total, 23 of them gold. No other athlete has more Olympic medals.
22146.m: With 28 medals, Michael Phelps is the most successful Olympian.

22147.q: Which Swede has improved the pole vault world record again and again since 2020 (as of 2026)?
22147.e: Since 2020 Armand “Mondo” Duplantis has improved the world record by one centimetre at a time. In March 2026 he cleared 6.31 metres in Uppsala, which is the world record (as of October 2026).
22147.m: Armand Duplantis holds the pole vault world record.

22148.q: Roughly how far is the men's long jump world record?
22148.e: Mike Powell jumped 8.95 metres in Tokyo in 1991. This world record still stands today (as of 2026).
22148.m: The men's long jump world record is just under 9 metres.

22149.q: Roughly how high is the men's world record in the high jump?
22149.e: Javier Sotomayor from Cuba jumped 2.45 metres in 1993. That is clearly higher than most people are tall.
22149.m: The high jump world record is 2.45 metres.

22150.q: How many gold medals did Michael Phelps win at the 2008 Olympic Games in Beijing?
22150.e: Michael Phelps won eight gold medals in Beijing in 2008. He beat Mark Spitz, who had won seven gold medals at a single Games in 1972.
22150.m: No athlete has won more gold medals at a single Games than Michael Phelps in 2008.

22151.q: Roughly how fast is the women's 100 metres world record?
22151.e: Florence Griffith-Joyner from the USA ran the 100 metres in 10.49 seconds in 1988. Nobody has matched this time to this day (as of 2026).
22151.m: The women's 100 metres world record is about 10.5 seconds.

22152.q: What is warming up before sport for?
a: It prepares the muscles, heart and circulation for the effort
It makes the muscles stronger straight away
22152.e: When you warm up, your body temperature, pulse and blood flow go up. This helps the muscles work better and lowers the risk of injury.
22152.m: Warming up prepares the body for the effort.

22153.q: What is it called when the body recovers after training to a level above its previous performance?
22153.e: After exercise the body recovers and builds up a little more performance than before. This is called supercompensation.
22153.m: Through supercompensation the body becomes fitter after recovery.

22154.q: Using the rule of thumb 220 minus age, roughly what is the maximum heart rate of a 12-year-old?
22154.e: The sum is 220 minus 12, which makes 208. The rule of thumb only gives a rough guide.
22154.m: You can roughly estimate maximum heart rate as 220 minus your age.

22155.q: What is a type of training called in which periods of effort and recovery alternate regularly?
22155.e: In interval training, intense phases are followed by short breaks. This means you can train at high intensity more often.
22155.m: In interval training, effort and rest alternate.

22156.q: Why are rest days important in training?
a: Because the body adapts and gets stronger during recovery
Because muscles only use energy when resting
Because then you can skip the warm-up
Because you get more sore muscles on rest days
22156.e: Improvement happens in the recovery phase after training. Without enough breaks, there is a risk of overtraining.
22156.m: Without enough recovery you will not get better.

22157.q: What are you measuring if you count your pulse in the morning straight after waking up?
22157.e: The resting heart rate is the heart rate when completely at rest. In well-trained endurance athletes it is often lower than in untrained people.
22157.m: A low resting heart rate is often a sign of good endurance.

22158.q: A runner trains three times a week for 40 minutes each time. How many hours is that in four weeks?
22158.e: Each week it is 3 times 40, which equals 120 minutes. In four weeks that makes 480 minutes, so 8 hours.
22158.m: Training time is easy to add up over the weeks.

22159.e: The marathon distance is exactly 42.195 kilometres. This length was fixed in 1921.

22160.q: What does “aerobic” mean when muscles produce energy?
22160.e: During aerobic exercise the muscle gets enough oxygen to produce energy. This is the case when running calmly for a long time.
22160.m: Aerobic exercise happens with enough oxygen.

22161.q: What do you feel when you run very fast and your muscles no longer get enough oxygen?
a: The muscles feel heavy and burn
22161.e: Without enough oxygen the muscle produces energy in an emergency way. This creates lactate, and the muscles tire quickly.
22161.m: If you go too fast, your muscles quickly get tired.

22162.q: Which three disciplines make up a triathlon, in this order?
22162.e: A triathlon starts with swimming, then comes cycling and finally a run. The changeovers count towards the total time.
22162.m: In a triathlon you swim first, then cycle and run at the end.

22163.q: Which part of the blood carries oxygen to the muscles?
22163.e: Red blood cells contain haemoglobin, which binds oxygen. This is how oxygen gets from the lungs to the muscles.
22163.m: Red blood cells bring oxygen to the muscles.

22164.q: How does the heart change through regular endurance training?
a: It pumps more blood with each beat
It needs more oxygen at rest
22164.e: A trained heart becomes stronger and pumps more blood with each beat. That is why it needs fewer beats at rest.
22164.m: Endurance training makes the heart stronger.

22165.q: What distance do you run in a half marathon?
22165.e: A half marathon is exactly half the marathon distance. 42.195 divided by 2 makes 21.0975 kilometres.
22165.m: A half marathon is half as long as a marathon.

22166.q: What is the ability to develop force against resistance as quickly as possible called, for example when taking off for a jump?
22166.e: You need explosive strength for sprinting, jumping and throwing, for example. The muscle has to build up a lot of force in a short time.
22166.m: Explosive strength is important for jumps and sprints.

22167.q: What is the greatest force a muscle can produce on purpose called?
22167.e: Maximum strength is the highest force you can produce against a resistance. It is important in weightlifting, for example.
22167.m: Maximum strength is the highest force a muscle can produce.

22168.q: What do you mainly train when you do lots of repetitions with a light weight?
22168.e: Lots of repetitions with little weight improve the ability to keep up a force for a long time. This is called strength endurance.
22168.m: Lots of repetitions with little weight train strength endurance.

22169.q: Which muscle bends the arm at the elbow joint?
22169.e: The biceps is at the front of the upper arm and bends the elbow. Its opposite muscle, the triceps, straightens the arm again.
22169.m: The biceps bends the arm and the triceps straightens it.

22170.q: What is a strength exercise called in which you hold a position without moving, for example the forearm plank?
22170.e: In an isometric exercise the muscle tenses without changing its length. The forearm plank is a well-known example.
22170.m: In isometric exercises you hold a position without moving.

22171.q: Which two disciplines are there in Olympic weightlifting?
22171.e: Weightlifting has the snatch and the clean and jerk. In the snatch the bar is lifted over the head in one movement.
22171.m: Olympic weightlifting has the snatch and the clean and jerk.

22172.q: Which muscle group is mainly trained by squats?
22172.e: In a squat it is mainly the thigh and bottom muscles that work. A straight back is important.
22172.m: Squats mainly strengthen the legs and bottom.

22173.q: Why should children and teenagers start strength training with their own body weight?
a: So they learn the right technique and don't overload their joints
Because body weight is heavier than dumbbells
Because muscles only grow from age 20
Because strength training is forbidden for teenagers
22173.e: Exercises with your own body weight train technique and protect growing joints. Extra weight is only added gradually.
22173.m: In strength training, clean technique comes before heavy weight.

22273.q: Who wrote down many well-known German fairy tales?
22273.e: Jacob and Wilhelm Grimm collected fairy tales about 200 years ago and published them as a book.
22273.m: The Brothers Grimm collected many fairy tales.

22274.q: Which animal does Little Red Riding Hood meet in the forest?
22274.e: The wolf questions Little Red Riding Hood and then runs quickly to her grandmother’s house.
22274.m: Little Red Riding Hood meets the wolf in the forest.

22275.q: How many dwarfs live together in the fairy tale “Snow White”?
22275.e: Snow White finds the little house of seven dwarfs in the forest and is allowed to live with them.
22275.m: Snow White lives with seven dwarfs.

22276.q: Who lives in the gingerbread house in “Hansel and Gretel”?
22276.e: The witch lures the children with her sweet house. In the end Gretel outwits the witch.
22276.m: A wicked witch lives in the gingerbread house.

22277.q: How long does Sleeping Beauty sleep in the fairy tale?
22277.e: A wise woman who was not invited to the feast curses the princess. She pricks herself on a spindle and sleeps for a hundred years.
22277.m: Sleeping Beauty sleeps for a hundred years.

22278.q: What does the prince climb up into the tower in the fairy tale “Rapunzel”?
22278.e: Rapunzel lets her very long hair down from the window so that someone can climb up.
22278.m: Rapunzel lets her long hair down from the tower.

22279.q: Which animal is one of the Town Musicians of Bremen?
22279.e: The four animals are a donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster. They want to make music in Bremen.
22279.m: The Town Musicians of Bremen are a donkey, a dog, a cat and a rooster.

22280.q: What does Rumpelstiltskin spin out of straw?
22280.e: The little man helps the miller’s daughter and spins straw into gold. In return he demands a high price.
22280.m: Rumpelstiltskin can spin straw into gold.

22281.q: Who wrote the books about Pippi Longstocking?
22281.e: Astrid Lindgren was a writer from Sweden. Pippi first appeared in 1945.

22282.q: What is the name of Pippi Longstocking’s little monkey?
22282.e: Mr Nilsson is a little monkey and lives with Pippi in Villa Villekulla.
22282.m: Pippi’s monkey is called Mr Nilsson.

22283.e: Johanna Spyri was a Swiss writer from the canton of Zurich. “Heidi” is world-famous.
22283.m: The Swiss writer Johanna Spyri wrote “Heidi”.

22284.q: Where does Heidi live with her grandfather?
22284.e: Heidi lives with the Alm-Uncle in a hut high up in the mountains of the Grisons.
22284.m: Heidi lives with her grandfather on the Alpine pasture.

22285.q: What is the name of Heidi’s friend who uses a wheelchair?
22285.e: Heidi meets Clara in Frankfurt. Later Clara visits her in the mountains.
22285.m: Heidi’s friend Clara uses a wheelchair.

22286.q: What does Ursli in “A Bell for Ursli” want for the Chalandamarz procession?
22286.e: Ursli only gets a small bell. So he fetches a big bell from the family’s summer hut up the mountain.

22287.q: What does the very hungry caterpillar become in the end?
22287.e: The caterpillar eats a lot, builds itself a cocoon and comes out as a colourful butterfly. The book is by Eric Carle.
22287.m: The very hungry caterpillar turns into a butterfly.

22288.q: What does the Rainbow Fish give away to the other fish in the picture book?
22288.e: The Rainbow Fish learns that sharing makes you happy. The book is by Marcus Pfister from Bern.
22288.m: The Rainbow Fish shares his shiny scales.

22289.q: Which small animal takes a walk through the wood in the picture book “The Gruffalo”?
22289.e: The clever mouse invents the Gruffalo to frighten dangerous animals.
22289.m: In “The Gruffalo”, a clever mouse is the main character.

22290.q: What is the name of the locomotive in “Jim Button and Luke the Engine Driver”?
22290.e: Jim and Luke travel out into the world from the island of Lummerland with the locomotive Emma. The book is by Michael Ende.

22291.q: What makes Asterix and the other Gauls strong?
22291.e: The druid Getafix brews the magic potion. Anyone who drinks it becomes very strong for a short time.
22291.m: The magic potion makes the Gauls strong.

22292.q: What is the name of Obelix’s little dog?
22292.e: Dogmatix is a little white dog. He does not like trees being cut down.
22292.m: Obelix has a little dog called Dogmatix.

22293.q: Why is Obelix not allowed to drink any more magic potion?
a: He fell into it as a baby
He is too old for it
22293.e: Because Obelix fell into the cauldron as a small child, he is strong for ever.
22293.m: Obelix has been strong for ever since he was little.

22294.q: What kind of animal is Snowy in “The Adventures of Tintin”?
22294.e: Snowy is a white fox terrier and goes with the reporter Tintin on all his adventures. He was created by Hergé from Belgium.

22295.q: What is the name of Lucky Luke’s horse?
22295.e: Jolly Jumper is a clever horse. He can even play chess.

22296.q: What are the names of Donald Duck’s three nephews?
22296.e: The three little ducks often stay with their Uncle Donald in Duckburg.
22296.m: Donald’s nephews are called Huey, Dewey and Louie.

22297.q: What are the shapes in a comic called that show what a character says?
22297.e: Speech bubbles show what a character says. A little point shows who is speaking.
22297.m: Speech bubbles show what comic characters say.

22298.e: The little Smurfs are blue and usually wear white hats. They were created by the Belgian artist Peyo.

22299.q: Which food does Garfield the cat especially love?
22299.e: Garfield is a lazy, fat cat. He loves lasagne and does not like Mondays at all.

22300.q: What kind of animal is the Swiss children’s book character Globi?
22300.e: Globi is a blue parrot with a cap and checked trousers. He has been around since 1932.
22300.m: Globi is a blue parrot from Switzerland.

22301.q: What is the name of Walt Disney’s first full-length animated film?
22301.e: The film came out in cinemas in 1937. Before that, Disney had only made short cartoons.
22301.m: Disney’s first full-length animated film was “Snow White”.

22302.q: What is the name of the lion cub in “The Lion King”?
22302.e: Simba is the son of King Mufasa and later becomes king himself.
22302.m: Simba is the young lion in “The Lion King”.

22303.q: What kind of animal is Pumbaa in “The Lion King”?
22303.e: Pumbaa is a funny warthog and a good friend of Timon.

22304.q: What is the snowman’s name in the film “Frozen”?
22304.e: Olaf is a cheerful snowman. He dreams of experiencing summer one day.
22304.m: The funny snowman is called Olaf.

22305.q: What kind of fish is Nemo in the film “Finding Nemo”?
22305.e: Nemo is an orange and white striped clownfish. His father searches the whole ocean for him.

22306.q: What is the cowboy’s name in the film “Toy Story”?
22306.e: Woody is a cowboy doll and the favourite toy of a boy called Andy.
22306.m: The cowboy in “Toy Story” is called Woody.

22308.q: What is the bear’s name in the film “The Jungle Book”?
22308.e: Baloo is an easy-going bear and a friend of the boy Mowgli.
22308.m: In “The Jungle Book” the bear is called Baloo.

22309.q: How is movement created in a cartoon?
a: Many pictures shown quickly one after another
One picture is shown for a long time
22309.e: Each picture is a little different. If you show them quickly one after the other, it looks as if everything is moving.
22309.m: Many quick pictures one after another make movement.

22310.q: What is the name of Maya the Bee’s best friend?
22310.e: Willy is an easy-going drone and goes with Maya on her adventures.
22310.m: Maya the Bee has a friend called Willy.

22311.q: What happens to Pinocchio’s nose when he lies?
22311.e: Pinocchio is a wooden puppet. Every time he lies, his nose grows.
22311.m: Pinocchio’s nose grows with every lie.

22312.q: What colour is Shrek the ogre?
22312.e: Shrek is a big green ogre. He lives in a swamp.

22313.e: The Minions are small yellow creatures with goggles and blue dungarees.
22313.m: The Minions are small and yellow.

22314.q: What does Paddington Bear like to eat most?
22314.e: Paddington comes from Peru to London. He always keeps a marmalade sandwich under his hat.

22315.q: What does Mary Poppins use to fly through the air?
22315.e: The nanny Mary Poppins floats down from the sky with her umbrella.
22315.m: Mary Poppins flies with her umbrella.

22316.q: What is WALL-E in the film of the same name?
22316.e: WALL-E is a small robot. He clears up the rubbish on Earth.
22316.m: WALL-E is a small tidying-up robot.

22317.q: What kind of character is Lightning McQueen in the film “Cars”?
22317.e: Lightning McQueen is a red racing car with the number 95.
22317.m: Lightning McQueen is a red racing car.

22318.q: What does the little elephant Dumbo use to fly?
22318.e: Dumbo has huge ears. At first he is laughed at, but then he flies through the air with them.
22318.m: Dumbo flies with his big ears.

22319.q: What is Remy the rat especially good at in the film “Ratatouille”?
22319.e: Remy dreams of becoming a chef. In Paris he secretly cooks in a restaurant.
22319.m: Remy the rat is a good cook.

22320.q: Which film character never wants to grow up?
22320.e: Peter Pan lives in Neverland and wants to stay a child for ever. He can even fly.
22320.m: Peter Pan wants to stay a child for ever.

22321.q: Which character did the Swiss actor Bruno Ganz play in the 2015 film “Heidi”?
22321.e: Bruno Ganz was a famous Swiss actor. He played Heidi’s grandfather, the Alm-Uncle.

22322.q: What is the name of the little polar bear in Hans de Beer’s books and films?
22322.e: The little polar bear Lars has many adventures at the North Pole with his friends.
22322.m: The little polar bear is called Lars.

22323.q: What does the label “from age 6” on a cinema film mean?
22323.e: The age rating shows from what age a film is suitable.
22323.m: The age rating shows who a film is suitable for.

22324.q: What is the list at the end of a film with everyone who worked on it called?
22324.e: The end credits show the names of all the people who helped make the film.
22324.m: The end credits show the names of everyone involved.

22325.q: What is the person who is in charge of making a film called?
22325.e: The director decides how the film is shot and helps the actors.
22325.m: The director is in charge of making a film.

22326.q: Who is Vicky in “Vicky the Viking”?
22326.e: Vicky is small but very clever. He helps the strong men with good ideas.
22326.m: Vicky is a clever Viking boy.

22327.q: What does the Sams have on its face?
22327.e: With each blue dot, the Sams can grant a wish. Then the dot disappears.
22327.m: The Sams grants wishes with its blue dots.

22328.q: Which country does the animated film “My Neighbour Totoro” come from?
22328.e: The film came out in Japan in 1988. Totoro is a big, fluffy forest creature.
22328.m: “My Neighbour Totoro” is a film from Japan.

22329.q: Which country does the plasticine character Pingu come from?
22329.e: Pingu was created by the Swiss Otmar Gutmann. The little penguin speaks a made-up language.
22329.m: Pingu is an animated character from Switzerland.

22330.q: What are the characters Wallace and Gromit made of?
22330.e: For every movement, the plasticine figures are moved a tiny bit and photographed again.
22330.m: Wallace and Gromit are plasticine figures.

22331.q: What is the name of Mario’s brother in the video games?
22331.e: Luigi wears a green cap and is a little taller than Mario.

22332.q: What do you have to do in the game “Tetris”?
22332.e: You turn and move the falling blocks so that full rows are formed. Full rows disappear.
22332.m: In “Tetris” you arrange falling blocks into rows.

22333.q: Who chases the game character Pac-Man?
22333.e: Pac-Man eats dots in a maze and has to avoid the colourful ghosts.

22334.q: What colour is the Pokémon Pikachu?
22334.e: Pikachu is yellow, with red cheeks and long ears with black tips.

22335.q: What is the world in the game “Minecraft” made of?
22335.e: Everything in Minecraft is built from blocks. You can break them up and put them down again.

22336.q: What kind of animal is the game character Sonic?
22336.e: Sonic is a blue hedgehog and very fast.
22336.m: Sonic is a fast blue hedgehog.

22337.q: What do you do in the game “Mario Kart”?
22337.e: In “Mario Kart”, well-known characters race against each other in little racing cars.

22338.q: What does the PEGI number on a game box show?
22338.e: PEGI is an age label used in Europe. The number tells you from what age a game is suitable.
22338.m: The PEGI number shows the right age for a game.

22340.q: What kind of animal is Donkey Kong?
22340.e: Donkey Kong is a big gorilla with a red tie. He loves bananas.

22341.q: Which country does the company Nintendo come from?
22341.e: Nintendo has its headquarters in Kyoto in Japan.
22341.m: Nintendo is a company from Japan.

22342.e: The first PlayStation came out in Japan in 1994. It is made by the company Sony.

22343.e: Microsoft brought out the first Xbox in 2001.

a: A console for playing on the go
22344.e: The Game Boy came out in 1989. You hold it in your hand and can play anywhere.
22344.m: The Game Boy is a small games console for playing on the go.

22345.q: What is the device you hold in your hand to control a console called?
22345.e: The controller has buttons and little sticks that you use to move the game character.
22345.m: You use the controller to control a game.

22346.q: What is special about the Nintendo Switch?
a: You can play on the TV and on the go
22346.e: You can connect the Switch to the TV or take it out and play on the go.
22346.m: You can use the Switch at home and on the go.

22347.q: How do you control many games on the Wii console?
22347.e: The Wii came out in 2006. You move the remote, for example like a tennis racket.
22347.m: On the Wii you control games with movements.

22348.q: What do you usually connect a home console to?
22348.e: The console sends the picture to the television. That way you see the game in a big size.
22348.m: A home console shows the game on the television.

22349.q: What did the company Nintendo make before there were video games?
22349.e: Nintendo was founded in 1889 and first made Japanese playing cards.

22350.q: Which console came out in 2025 as the successor to the Nintendo Switch?
22350.e: The Nintendo Switch 2 went on sale in June 2025.

22351.q: What do you call a film that is meant to make you laugh a lot?
22351.e: A comedy is funny and usually has a happy ending.

22352.q: What do you call films about cowboys in the Wild West?
22352.e: Westerns are usually set long ago in North America. There are horses, cowboys and small towns.
22352.m: In a western, cowboys ride through the Wild West.

22353.q: What do you call films about the future and journeys into space?
22353.e: Science fiction films show made-up technology, spaceships and alien planets.
22353.m: Science fiction tells stories about the future and space.

22354.q: What do you call a film in which the characters sing a lot?
22354.e: In a musical, the story is told with songs and dance.
22354.m: In a musical there is a lot of singing and dancing.

22355.q: What do you call a film that shows real animals or people?
22355.e: A documentary shows real life, for example animals in nature.
22355.m: A documentary shows the real world.

22356.q: What are the first films without sound called?
22356.e: In the early days, picture and sound could not yet be recorded and played together. That is why words were shown on cards in the picture.
22356.m: The first films were silent films.

22357.q: What is a crime film about?
a: There is a lot of singing
22357.e: In a crime film, detectives or police officers look for clues and solve a case.
22357.m: In a crime film a case is solved.

22358.q: What do you call films with magic, dragons and magical creatures?
22358.e: Fantasy films are often set in made-up worlds where there is magic.
22358.m: Fantasy films have magic and dragons.

22359.q: What do you call films with exciting journeys and treasure hunts?
22359.e: In an adventure film, the heroes go on dangerous journeys to faraway places.
22359.m: In an adventure film, heroes go on exciting journeys.

22360.q: What do you call films whose characters are drawn or made on a computer?
22360.e: No real actors appear in an animated film. The characters are drawn, modelled in clay or designed on a computer.
22360.m: Animated films have drawn or animated characters.

22361.q: What does William Tell shoot off his son’s head?
22361.e: The bailiff Gessler forces Tell to take this shot. Tell hits it and his son is unharmed.
22361.m: William Tell shot an apple off his son’s head.

22362.q: Which weapon does William Tell shoot with in the legend?
22362.e: The crossbow shoots short arrows called bolts.
22362.m: William Tell shot with a crossbow.

22363.q: What were the people of Altdorf supposed to salute in the Tell legend?
22363.e: The bailiff hung his hat on a pole. Tell walked past without saluting it.
22363.m: Tell refused to salute the bailiff’s hat.

22364.q: In the legend, which animal did the people of Uri send across the Devil’s Bridge first?
22364.e: The Devil wanted the first soul to cross the bridge. The people of Uri tricked him with a billy goat.
22364.m: The people of Uri tricked the Devil with a billy goat.

22365.q: What does the Pied Piper of Hamelin use to lure the rats out of the town?
22365.e: The Pied Piper plays his pipe, and all the rats follow him out of the town.
22365.m: The Pied Piper lures the rats with his pipe music.

22366.q: What does the fox want in the fable of the fox and the crow?
22366.e: The fox praises the crow until it sings. As it does, the cheese falls out of its beak.
22366.m: The clever fox gets the cheese by flattery.

22367.q: Who wins the race against the hare in the fable?
22367.e: The hare is fast but takes a break and falls asleep. The slow tortoise just keeps going.
22367.m: Slow and steady wins the race.

22368.q: In the fable, which animal collects supplies for the winter during the summer?
22368.e: The ant works hard while the grasshopper only makes music. In winter the ant has enough to eat.
22368.m: If you plan ahead, you have enough in winter.

22369.q: What was the name of the famous writer of fables from ancient Greece?
22369.e: Aesop lived over 2500 years ago. Many of his fables are still told today.
22369.m: Aesop is the best-known writer of fables.

22370.q: What often comes at the end of a fable?
22370.e: In fables, animals talk like people. At the end, a moral shows what you can learn from it.
22370.m: A fable often ends with a moral.

22371.q: Which brothers were the first to show films to a paying audience in Paris in 1895?
22371.e: Auguste and Louis Lumière showed short films for an entrance fee in a Paris café on 28 December 1895. That evening is seen as the birth of cinema.
22371.m: The Lumière brothers are seen as the inventors of cinema.

22372.q: What was new in cinema at the end of the 1920s?
a: Sound, so you could hear the characters speak
22372.e: In 1927, “The Jazz Singer” was one of the first films with spoken scenes to reach cinemas. Before that, films were silent and music was played live in the cinema.
22372.m: The age of sound films began at the end of the 1920s.

22373.q: Which silent film star became famous for the character of the Tramp with a bowler hat and walking stick?
22373.e: From 1914, Charlie Chaplin played the Tramp, a poor wanderer with a bowler hat, a cane and shoes that were too big. The character became known all over the world.
22373.m: Charlie Chaplin is one of the most famous comedians of the silent film era.

22374.q: Georges Méliès was a magician before he made “A Trip to the Moon” in 1902. What is he famous for in film as a result?
a: Early film tricks and special effects
22374.e: Méliès used his experience as a magician and invented many early film tricks. In “A Trip to the Moon”, a rocket lands in the Moon’s eye.
22374.m: Georges Méliès is seen as the father of special effects in film.

22375.q: What does the trophy you win at the Oscars look like?
a: A golden figure of a man
22375.e: The Oscar is a golden figure of a man with a sword. The Golden Lion, Golden Bear and Palme d’Or are prizes of the film festivals in Venice, Berlin and Cannes.
22375.m: The Oscar is a golden figure.

22376.q: In which canton does the film festival with screenings on the Piazza Grande take place?
22376.e: The Locarno Film Festival has existed since 1946. Every August, thousands of people watch films in the open air on the Piazza Grande in Locarno.
22376.m: The Locarno Film Festival in Ticino is the best-known in Switzerland.

22377.q: Which city does the film district of Hollywood belong to?
22377.e: Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles in California. From around 1910, many film companies moved there because there was lots of sun and cheap land.
22377.m: Hollywood is a district of Los Angeles and the centre of the US film industry.

22378.q: Which German silent film from 1927 shows a huge city of the future with a machine-man?
22378.e: “Metropolis” by Fritz Lang is one of the first great science fiction films. Today it is part of UNESCO’s Memory of the World.
22378.m: “Metropolis” is a milestone of science fiction film.

22379.q: How many single pictures per second does a classic cinema film show?
22379.e: Since the start of sound films, 24 frames per second has become the standard for cinema. Because the pictures change so quickly, our eyes see smooth movement.
22379.m: A cinema film normally shows 24 pictures per second.

22380.q: The Swiss film “Journey of Hope” won an Oscar in 1991. What is it about?
a: A family trying to flee to Switzerland
A dog looking for its way home
22380.e: Xavier Koller’s film tells the story of a Kurdish family trying to enter Switzerland illegally. It won the Oscar for best foreign-language film.
22380.m: Xavier Koller won an Oscar for Switzerland with “Journey of Hope”.

22381.q: What is the name of the lion cub in “The Lion King” who is meant to follow his father Mufasa onto the throne?
22381.e: Simba is the son of King Mufasa. After his father’s death he runs away, but later returns and becomes king of the Pride Lands.
22381.m: Simba is the hero of “The Lion King”.

22382.q: Which director made the dinosaur film “Jurassic Park” in 1993?
22382.e: Steven Spielberg filmed Michael Crichton’s novel. The film set new standards for computer-animated animals.
22382.m: Steven Spielberg is one of the most successful directors in film history.

22383.q: Who created the “Star Wars” films and directed the first one in 1977?
22383.e: George Lucas wrote the story and made the first film in 1977, which was later given the title “Episode IV: A New Hope”. The series became one of the most successful of all.
22383.m: George Lucas is the creator of “Star Wars”.

22384.q: Which film is (as of 2026) the highest-grossing film of all time worldwide?
22384.e: James Cameron’s “Avatar” from 2009 earned around 2.9 billion US dollars worldwide. That puts it (as of 2026) at the top of the list.
22384.m: “Avatar” is (as of 2026) the most successful film at the box office.

22385.q: Which vehicle does Doc Brown turn into a time machine in “Back to the Future”?
22385.e: Doc Brown turns a DeLorean sports car into a time machine. At 88 miles per hour, the car travels through time.
22385.m: In “Back to the Future” people travel through time in a converted car.

22386.q: What is the name of Dorothy’s little dog in the 1939 film “The Wizard of Oz”?
22386.e: Toto goes with Dorothy on her journey through the Land of Oz. The film is one of the best-known early colour films.
22386.m: Dorothy’s dog Toto is always with her in “The Wizard of Oz”.

22387.q: In the film “Jurassic Park”, where does the dinosaurs’ DNA come from?
22387.e: In the film, mosquitoes sucked dinosaur blood millions of years ago and were then trapped in tree resin. Scientists get the DNA from the blood.
22387.m: In “Jurassic Park” the dinosaur DNA comes from mosquitoes in amber.

22388.q: In “Star Wars”, who is Luke Skywalker’s father?
22388.e: In “The Empire Strikes Back” (1980), Darth Vader reveals that he is Luke’s father. He used to be called Anakin Skywalker.
22388.m: Darth Vader is Luke Skywalker’s father.

22389.q: What is the film character Indiana Jones’s job?
22389.e: Indiana Jones is a professor of archaeology and searches for famous treasures on adventurous journeys. He is played by Harrison Ford.
22389.m: Indiana Jones is an adventurous archaeologist.

22390.q: What is the name of the founder of the studio that brought out Mickey Mouse?
22390.e: Walt Disney founded a cartoon studio with his brother Roy in 1923. Mickey Mouse became the studio’s best-known character.
22390.m: Walt Disney founded one of the most famous film studios in the world.

22391.q: Which studio made the animated films “Ratatouille” and “Up”?
22391.e: Pixar Animation Studios from California specialises in computer-animated films. Since 2006 Pixar has belonged to Disney.
22391.m: Pixar is a studio for computer-animated films.

22392.q: In which country does the well-known animation studio Ghibli have its headquarters?
22392.e: Studio Ghibli was founded in Tokyo in 1985. Its hand-drawn films are loved all over the world.
22392.m: Studio Ghibli is an animation studio from Japan.

22393.q: In which country is Aardman, the studio that created “Shaun the Sheep”?
22393.e: Aardman Animations is based in Bristol in England. The studio is famous for its plasticine figures.
22393.m: Aardman is an English studio for plasticine films.

22394.q: Which animal roars at the start of films by the studio Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer (MGM)?
22394.e: The roaring lion has been MGM’s trademark for almost 100 years. Over time, several different lions have been filmed.
22394.m: At MGM a lion roars before every film.

22395.q: Why do film studios shoot many scenes in large halls instead of outdoors?
a: Because light, sound and weather can be controlled there
Because cameras do not work outside
Because halls are cheaper than cameras
22395.e: In a studio hall, neither rain nor traffic noise gets in the way. The team can set up the lighting and scenery exactly as the scene needs. A famous example is Babelsberg Studio near Berlin.
22395.m: In a studio, light, sound and weather can be controlled.

22396.q: Which company bought Lucasfilm, and with it the rights to “Star Wars”, in 2012?
22396.e: Disney took over Lucasfilm in 2012 for around 4 billion US dollars. After that, new “Star Wars” films and series were made.
22396.m: Since 2012, “Star Wars” has belonged to Disney.

22397.q: Which studio made the animated film “Shrek” in 2001?
22397.e: With “Shrek”, DreamWorks Animation put a cheeky ogre at the centre of the story. The film became a successful series.
22397.m: “Shrek” comes from the studio DreamWorks Animation.

22398.q: Which studio created the yellow Minions?
22398.e: The Minions first appeared in 2010 in the film “Despicable Me” by the studio Illumination. Later they got their own films.
22398.m: The Minions come from the studio Illumination.

22399.q: What is the big film industry in Mumbai (India) called?
22399.e: The name Bollywood is made from Bombay, the former name of Mumbai, and Hollywood. India makes a great many films every year.

22400.q: Which Disney film from 1937 was the studio’s first full-length animated film?
a: Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs
22400.e: “Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs” came out in cinemas in 1937. Many thought the project was too risky, but it was a huge success.
22400.m: In 1937, “Snow White” was Disney’s first full-length animated film.

22401.q: Which 1995 film was the first full-length cinema film to be animated entirely on a computer?
22401.e: In “Toy Story”, toys such as Woody and Buzz Lightyear come to life. All the pictures in the film were made on a computer.
22401.m: “Toy Story” is the first fully computer-animated cinema film.

22402.q: What is the animation technique called in which figures made of plasticine or wood are moved slightly and photographed picture by picture?
22402.e: In stop motion, each figure is moved a tiny bit after every photo. If you play the photos quickly one after another, it seems to move.
22402.m: In stop motion, movement is created from many single photos.

22403.e: Hayao Miyazaki’s film won the Oscar for best animated film in 2003. It tells the story of a girl in a world full of spirits.
22403.m: Hayao Miyazaki is one of the best-known animation directors in the world.

22404.q: What is the name of Elsa’s sister in the film “Frozen”?
22404.e: Anna sets out to find her sister Elsa, who has frozen the kingdom with her ice powers. The film came out in 2013.
22404.m: Anna and Elsa are the sisters from “Frozen”.

22405.q: Which Swiss stop-motion film by Claude Barras was nominated for an Oscar in 2017?
22405.e: “My Life as a Courgette” (2016) tells the story of a boy in a children’s home. The film was nominated for the Oscar for best animated film.
22405.m: With “My Life as a Courgette”, Claude Barras made an award-winning Swiss animated film.

22406.q: What is the name of the 1928 cartoon in which Mickey Mouse whistles at the wheel of a steamboat?
22406.e: “Steamboat Willie” was one of the first cartoons with synchronised sound. In it Mickey steers a steamboat until Captain Pete chases him off the bridge.
22406.m: Mickey Mouse became famous in 1928 with “Steamboat Willie”.

22407.q: What kind of animal is Gromit in the plasticine films “Wallace & Gromit”?
22407.e: Gromit is the clever dog of the inventor Wallace. He never speaks, but shows what he thinks with his eyes and forehead.

22408.q: Which film was the first to win the Oscar for best animated film in 2002?
22408.e: The category of best animated film was introduced in 2002. “Shrek” beat “Monsters, Inc.” and “Jimmy Neutron”.
22408.m: “Shrek” was the first winner of the Oscar for best animated film.

22409.q: Who is in charge of filming and tells the actors how to act?
22409.e: The director decides how the story is told and acted. The producer, on the other hand, mainly takes care of money and organisation.
22409.m: The director is in artistic charge of the filming.

22410.q: What is the text called in which the plot, scenes and dialogue of a film are written down?
22410.e: The script says who says what and what happens in each scene. It is the basis for filming.
22410.m: The script contains all the scenes and dialogue of a film.

22411.q: What do you call a series of drawn sketches that shows the individual shots before filming?
22411.e: A storyboard looks like a comic of the planned film. That way the team knows in advance what each shot should look like.
22411.m: A storyboard shows the film in advance as a series of drawings.

22412.q: What is a green background (green screen) used for when filming?
a: It is later replaced by another picture
It muffles the sound in the studio
It protects the camera from light
22412.e: The computer recognises the green colour and swaps it for any background. That way actors can seem to be in space or on a dragon.
22412.m: With a green screen you can swap the background afterwards.

22413.q: Why is the clapperboard snapped shut before a take?
a: So that picture and sound match up later
So that the actors calm down
So that the studio lights come on
22413.e: The clap can be heard in the sound and the snapping can be seen in the picture. During editing, both are lined up exactly. The scene and take number are also written on the clapperboard.
22413.m: The clapperboard helps fit picture and sound together exactly.

22414.q: What is the work called in which the filmed shots are chosen and put together into a film?
22414.e: In film editing, the editor chooses the best shots and puts them in order. This creates the film’s pace and suspense.
22414.m: In film editing, many shots become a finished film.

22415.q: What is it called when voice actors record a foreign film again in another language?
22415.e: In dubbing, voice actors speak the dialogue again to match the lip movements. With subtitles, on the other hand, the original sound stays.
22415.m: Dubbing puts a film into another language.

22416.q: What is the selection process called in which actors try out for a role?
22416.e: At a casting, applicants show how they would play a role. Then the team decides who gets the part.
22416.m: At a casting, the actors for a film are chosen.

22417.q: What are the people called who film dangerous scenes instead of the actors?
22417.e: Stunt performers are specially trained for falls, fights or car chases. Extras, on the other hand, are people in the background.
22417.m: Stunt performers take on the dangerous scenes in a film.

22418.q: What is a short advert called that shows clips from a new cinema film?
22418.e: A trailer is meant to make people curious about the film and is shown in cinemas or online before the film comes out. The end credits, on the other hand, show the names of those involved at the end.
22418.m: A trailer uses short clips to make you want to see a new film.

22419.q: Who wrote the books on which the “Harry Potter” films were based?
22419.e: The British author J. K. Rowling published seven books from 1997 to 2007. All of them were filmed between 2001 and 2011.
22419.m: The “Harry Potter” books are by J. K. Rowling.

22420.q: Which Swiss writer wrote the often-filmed “Heidi” books?
22420.e: Johanna Spyri published “Heidi’s Years of Learning and Travel” in 1880. The story has been translated into many languages and filmed again and again.

22421.q: In which country were Peter Jackson’s “The Lord of the Rings” films mainly shot?
22421.e: Peter Jackson comes from New Zealand and used the landscapes of his homeland for Middle-earth. The books were written by J. R. R. Tolkien.
22421.m: Middle-earth was filmed in New Zealand.

22422.q: Which country did Astrid Lindgren come from, whose books such as “Pippi Longstocking” have often been filmed?
22422.e: Astrid Lindgren lived in Sweden and wrote, among others, “Pippi Longstocking”, “Emil of Lönneberga” and “Ronia, the Robber’s Daughter”. Many of them were filmed in Sweden.
22422.m: Astrid Lindgren was a Swedish children’s author.

22423.q: Which German author wrote “The Neverending Story”, which was filmed in 1984?
22423.e: Michael Ende published the novel in 1979. In the film, Atreyu rides the luckdragon Falkor.
22423.m: “The Neverending Story” is by Michael Ende.

22424.q: How are Lisa and Lottie related in Erich Kästner’s often-filmed book “Lottie and Lisa”?
22424.e: The two girls meet by chance at a holiday home and realise they are twins. They swap places to bring their separated parents back together. The book was written by Erich Kästner.
22424.m: Lisa and Lottie are twins who were separated after birth.

22425.q: In the first Narnia film, through which object do the children get into the land of Narnia?
22425.e: At the back of an old wardrobe, Lucy discovers a snowy forest. The book by C. S. Lewis was filmed in 2005.
22425.m: You get into Narnia through a wardrobe.

22426.q: What is the name of the factory owner in Roald Dahl’s “Charlie and the Chocolate Factory”?
22426.e: Willy Wonka invites five children with golden tickets into his mysterious factory. The book was filmed in 1971 and 2005.
22426.m: Willy Wonka owns the famous chocolate factory.

22427.q: Which Swiss children’s book character from the Engadine was filmed in 2015 and looks for a big bell for Chalandamarz?
22427.e: The picture book “A Bell for Ursli” by Selina Chönz and Alois Carigiet came out in 1945. Xavier Koller filmed the story in 2015.
22427.m: Ursli is a famous children’s book character from the Engadine.

22428.q: Which author wrote “The Jungle Book”, which Disney made into a cartoon in 1967?
22428.e: Rudyard Kipling published the stories about the boy Mowgli in 1894. He was born in India, where the story is set.
22428.m: “The Jungle Book” is by Rudyard Kipling.

22429.q: Which country do the Asterix and Obelix comics come from?
22429.e: René Goscinny and Albert Uderzo created Asterix in France in 1959. The stories are set in a Gaulish village in Roman times.
22429.m: Asterix is a comic hero from France.

22430.q: Which Belgian artist created “The Adventures of Tintin”?
22430.e: Hergé’s real name was Georges Remi. His pen name comes from his initials R. G. pronounced in French.

22431.q: Which comic character is said to shoot faster than his own shadow?
22431.e: Lucky Luke is a lonesome cowboy in the Wild West. The Belgian artist Morris created him in 1946.
22431.m: Lucky Luke is the cowboy who draws faster than his shadow.

22433.q: Which planet does the comic hero Superman come from?
22433.e: As a baby, Superman was sent to Earth from his dying home planet Krypton. He first appeared in a comic book in 1938.
22433.m: Superman comes from the planet Krypton.

22434.q: Which comic writer created the character Spider-Man together with Steve Ditko?
22434.e: Stan Lee and Steve Ditko introduced Spider-Man in 1962. Behind the mask is the school pupil Peter Parker.
22434.m: Stan Lee helped create many famous superheroes.

22435.q: What is the shape in a comic called that shows what a character says?
22435.e: The speech bubble usually has a little point that shows which character is speaking. Thoughts are often shown in cloud-shaped bubbles.
22435.m: The speech bubble shows what a comic character says.

22436.q: In which direction is a Japanese manga traditionally read?
22436.e: Like Japanese books, manga are read from back to front and from right to left. Many translations keep this reading direction.
22436.m: A manga is read from right to left.

22437.q: What is the name of the city where Donald Duck and Scrooge McDuck live?
22437.e: The English name of the city is Duckburg. The German translator Erika Fuchs called it Entenhausen.

22438.q: Who drew the comic strip “Peanuts” with Snoopy and Charlie Brown?
22438.e: Charles M. Schulz drew “Peanuts” entirely on his own from 1950 to 2000. The strip appeared in thousands of newspapers worldwide.
22438.m: Snoopy and Charlie Brown were created by Charles M. Schulz.

22439.q: Which sport does the early 1972 video game “Pong” imitate?
22439.e: In “Pong”, two players each move a bar up and down and hit a dot back and forth. It was one of the first commercially successful arcade machines.
22439.m: “Pong” is an early video game based on table tennis.

22440.q: In which country was the game “Tetris” invented in 1984?
22440.e: The programmer Alexey Pajitnov developed “Tetris” in Moscow. You have to turn falling blocks so that full rows are formed.
22440.m: “Tetris” was invented in the Soviet Union.

22441.q: What was the game character Mario’s original job?
22441.e: Mario appeared in “Donkey Kong” in 1981 and became a plumber travelling through pipes in “Mario Bros.” (1983). His brother is called Luigi.
22441.m: Mario is a plumber by trade.

22442.q: For which company did Shigeru Miyamoto create the game characters Mario and Link?
22442.e: Shigeru Miyamoto has worked at Nintendo since 1977. Among other things, he created “Super Mario Bros.” and “The Legend of Zelda”.
22442.m: Mario and Link are Nintendo characters by Shigeru Miyamoto.

22443.q: Who chases Pac-Man around his maze?
22443.e: In the 1980 game, four coloured ghosts chase the yellow game character. After eating a power pellet, Pac-Man can turn the tables.
22443.m: Pac-Man has to flee from ghosts in the maze.

22444.q: What was special about Nintendo’s Game Boy, which came out in 1989?
a: It only worked on the TV
22444.e: The Game Boy was a portable games console with batteries and a small screen. Together with “Tetris” it sold extremely well.
22444.m: The Game Boy was a console for playing on the go.

22445.q: What type is the Pokémon Pikachu?
22445.e: Pikachu stores electricity in its red cheeks and attacks with lightning. The first Pokémon games came out in Japan in 1996.

22446.q: Which country does the game “Minecraft” come from?
22446.e: The Swedish programmer Markus Persson began developing it in 2009, and his company Mojang is based in Stockholm. In “Minecraft” you build worlds out of blocks.

22447.q: What were the first home games consoles connected to in the 1970s?
22447.e: The first home console, the Magnavox Odyssey from 1972, was connected to the television. A plastic sheet with the playing field was placed over the screen.
22447.m: The first home consoles ran on the television.

22448.q: What are video game machines called that people used to play with coins, mainly in amusement arcades?
22448.e: Arcade machines were very popular in the 1970s and 1980s. Many well-known games first came out as arcade machines and only later for consoles.
22448.m: Arcade machines are video games in amusement arcades.

22449.q: Which genre does a game belong to in which the character mainly jumps over platforms and obstacles?
22449.e: Such games are also called platformers or “jump and run” games. The character runs through levels and jumps over gaps and enemies.
22449.m: In a platform game the character jumps and runs through the levels.

22450.q: Which genre does the game “Mario Kart” belong to?
22450.e: In “Mario Kart”, characters race each other in little go-karts and collect items along the way. Light-hearted racing games like this are also called kart racers.

22451.q: Which genre does “Tetris” belong to, in which you cleverly arrange falling blocks?
22451.e: Puzzle games are about logic, skill and spatial thinking. You have to arrange shapes or pieces so that a task is solved.

22452.q: What does the abbreviation RPG stand for in computer games?
22452.e: In an RPG, or role-playing game, the character collects experience points and becomes stronger during the game.
22452.m: An RPG is a role-playing game in which the character develops.

22453.q: Which genre does a game like “SimCity”, in which you plan and run a city, belong to?
22453.e: In city-building games you put up houses, roads and services and have to manage your money and resources. If you plan well, the city grows.
22453.m: In a city-building game you plan and run a city or a realm.

22454.q: What do you call games with a large game world you can explore freely without a fixed route?
22454.e: In an open world, players decide for themselves where to go and which tasks to do first.
22454.m: In an open-world game you can explore the game world freely.

22455.q: In which genre do you mainly solve puzzles, collect items and talk to characters, often by clicking the mouse?
22455.e: In point-and-click adventures you point at things in the picture with the mouse and click. You often have to combine items cleverly to get further.
22455.m: In an adventure you make progress with puzzles and conversations.

22456.q: What is the difference between a turn-based strategy game and a real-time strategy game?
22456.e: In turn-based games you take your turn one after the other, a bit like chess. In real-time strategy games everyone acts at the same time.
22456.m: In a turn-based game each player takes a turn in order.

22457.q: What do you do in a rhythm game?
a: Make inputs in time with the music
22457.e: In rhythm games you have to press buttons, dance or clap exactly when the music calls for it. The more precisely you hit the beat, the more points you get.
22457.m: A rhythm game asks for inputs in time with the music.

22458.q: What do you call games that are mainly meant to teach knowledge, for example in maths or learning vocabulary?
22458.e: Learning games combine fun with practice, for example through points, levels or rewards. Quiz apps are also part of this.
22458.m: Learning games help you learn new things in a playful way.

22459.q: Who invented printing with movable metal letters in Mainz around 1450?
22459.e: Johannes Gutenberg cast single letters out of metal, which could be put together again and again. This made it possible to produce books much faster and more cheaply.
22459.m: Gutenberg’s printing made books available to many people.

22460.q: Which invention from 1876 made it possible to send the human voice along wires?
22460.e: Alexander Graham Bell patented the telephone in 1876. For the first time, people could talk directly to each other over long distances.
22460.m: Since 1876 the telephone has carried the voice along wires.

22461.q: At which research centre in Geneva was the World Wide Web invented in 1989?
22461.e: In 1989, the British physicist Tim Berners-Lee proposed a system of linked pages at CERN. This became the World Wide Web.
